summary: This is a VS Code development container configuration for a Quarto documentation project. It specifies how to set up a containerized development environment with Docker, configures Git SSH access, sets up code formatting and linting rules for various file types, and lists the VS Code extensions needed for the project.

explanations.3: This points to the Docker Compose file that defines the container services; VS Code will read this to know how to build and run the development container.
explanations.8: This sets up SSH authentication inside the container so Git commands can access private repositories using a specific SSH key, while accepting any host (since /dev/null ignores known_hosts).
explanations.10: This command runs once before attaching to the container; it creates a directory structure and a gitignore file to keep bash history persistent across container restarts without committing it to Git.
explanations.11: This runs after you connect to the container; it installs pre-commit hooks if the pre-commit tool exists, helping enforce code quality checks before commits.
explanations.40: This tells the spell-checker to validate words in English, French, and Dutch, so it won't flag correctly-spelled words in those languages as errors.
explanations.68: This tells VS Code to treat JSON files inside the resources folder as JSONC (JSON with Comments), so you can add comments in those files.
explanations.84: This configures custom code folding for Dockerfiles using region markers (lines with `# region` and `# endregion` comments), making it easier to collapse sections of the file.
explanations.109: This associates specific YAML files with JSON schema files so VS Code can provide autocomplete and validation tailored to Quarto and GitHub workflow configuration formats.
explanations.116: This customizes the VS Code window title to show the project name, whether it has unsaved changes, and remind you that you're working in a development container.
